title: Flow Over Force
hook: Some stuff feels like pushing a boulder uphill because you're pushing it in the wrong direction.
statement: Systems run best when they flow, not when you force them.
explainer: Forcing can get results for a while, but it costs you. When you work with your strengths and existing demand, the same output takes way less out of you.
sop: Name one area where you're pushing hard against resistance.
Score the Alignment and Friction there 1 to 10.
Figure out the cause: wrong timing, audience, format, or person.
Adjust so you're working with the demand, not against it.
Track output before and after. Aligned should feel easier.
equation_example: Alignment 8, Friction 5. 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6. Higher means you can keep this pace without burning out. Below 1, where friction beats alignment, is burnout on the way, even if output looks fine now.
question: Write down where you're forcing it right now and what going with the flow would look like.
closing_statement: Working with the current beats fighting it.
caption:
Principle Nº 106: Flow Over Force

Some stuff feels like pushing a boulder uphill because you're pushing it in the wrong direction.

Systems run best when they flow, not when you force them.

Your turn: Write down where you're forcing it right now and what going with the flow would look like.
